definitions.explanation: The standard verb for drinking liquids. Used for water, tea, coffee, alcohol, and any other beverages. Can also be used for taking medicine ({薬|くすり}を{飲|の}む).
Used for swallowing pills or capsules. Also used figuratively for accepting something difficult (e.g., {条件|じょうけん}を{飲|の}む - to swallow/accept conditions).

examples.japanese: コーヒーを{飲|の}みますか。
examples.english: Would you like to drink coffee?

examples.japanese: {薬|くすり}を{飲|の}んでください。

notes:
TRANSITIVITY: {他動詞|たどうし} (transitive). No pair verb. Pattern: Xを{飲|の}む (drink X).

ASPECT: ている indicates ongoing action. {飲|の}んでいる = 'is drinking.'

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{水|みず}を{飲|の}む (drink water)
・{薬|くすり}を{飲|の}む (take medicine)
・お{酒|さけ}を{飲|の}む (drink alcohol)
・{飲|の}み{物|もの} (beverage)

Godan verb with irregular te-form: む → んで.

Related: {食|た}べる (to eat).
